techniques.name: Accordion Expansion
techniques.does: A panel expands from a fixed edge while adjacent content moves aside.
use_when: Reveal detailed settings progressively.
Unfold code to explain its contents.

techniques.name: Action Sequence
techniques.does: One action finishes and the next begins, showing steps in order.
use_when: When showing procedure or pipeline steps in order
When a cause is followed by its result

techniques.name: Active Indicator Glide
techniques.does: The active underline or capsule glides to the newly selected tab.
use_when: Show selection moving between tabs.
Indicate the current menu location.

techniques.name: Adaptive Header Motion
techniques.does: A header hides or shrinks during scrolling and returns when direction changes.
use_when: Use this effect when you need to communicate: Frees content space while preserving navigation context.
Connect interaction states within a product demonstration.

techniques.name: Additive Dissolve
techniques.does: The bright colors of two scenes add together, brightening the middle before settling to the next scene.
use_when: To ease a light, airy scene change such as a memory, dream, or intro
To carry a product video from one screen to the next like spreading light

techniques.name: Additive Motion
techniques.does: A small wobble or rotation is layered on top of an element following a larger path.
use_when: Give an icon or card weight by letting it sway while it travels.
Bind several elements to one parent rig so they move together.

techniques.name: Aggregate Split and Merge
techniques.does: An aggregate mark splits into detailed marks, or detailed marks merge into one aggregate.
use_when: Use when you need to explain aggregate split and merge while preserving item identities and chart scales.
Use when the audience needs to follow the intermediate states rather than only compare final snapshots.

techniques.name: Ambient Glow
techniques.does: A blurred multicolor light shifts and brightens behind a surface.
use_when: Add a soft breathing backlight behind a product card.
Use a short repeating motion to communicate creates warm depth and a sense of continuing activity.

techniques.name: Ambient Particle Drift
techniques.does: Small, faint particles drift at different speeds.
use_when: Bring quiet life to empty space.
Suggest depth in a background.

techniques.name: Analog Medium Text
techniques.does: Chalk letters are written, then an eraser band passes over leaving a faint smudge.
use_when: Teaching content that writes a key concept and wipes it before the next
Class-toned video openers

techniques.name: Anchored Substitution
techniques.does: Each new item replaces the previous item at a shared anchor.
use_when: Use when explaining anchored substitution in a presentation or interactive view.
Use when viewers need to track corresponding items between states.

techniques.name: Animated Dithering
techniques.does: An image is drawn with limited colors and regular dot patterns, and the color levels animate.
use_when: To add texture in retro-game, indie, or illustrated brand videos
For a transition where an image comes to life from a dither pattern into full color

techniques.name: Animated Lighting
techniques.does: The color and intensity of light on a 3D object change, revealing different parts of it.
use_when: Sweep light across a product model's contours.
Change mood from cool to warm.
Reveal a subject as if switching on a light in the dark.

techniques.name: Annotation Callout
techniques.does: An animation that draws a leader line from a point on a chart and then reveals an annotation.
use_when: When highlighting a significant data point and its meaning
When adding a selection-rate annotation to a point on a completed chart

techniques.name: Annotation Tracking
techniques.does: Labels and leader lines follow a moving target with a fixed spatial relationship.
use_when: Explain causes and results using annotation tracking.
Present corresponding elements in a readable sequence within the same view.

techniques.name: Answer Streaming
techniques.does: An animation that reveals an answer in sequential token groups and gradually increases the opacity of each new group.
use_when: When revealing an AI answer in 10 groups every 0.18 seconds with a vermilion cursor block at the end
When showing the answer generation process and current output position

techniques.name: Anticipation
techniques.does: A brief movement in the opposite direction prepares the viewer for the main action.
use_when: Signal the launch direction of a character or icon.
Prepare the viewer's attention before a large movement.

techniques.name: Arcs
techniques.does: An object follows a curved trajectory instead of a straight line.
use_when: Explain the trajectory of a bouncing or thrown ball.
Create more fluid movement through space than a straight-line translation.

techniques.name: Arc Spinner
techniques.does: A rotating arc alternately lengthens and shortens.
use_when: Use when presenting arc spinner in a waiting or ambient scene.
Use for a compact status indicator with a stable surrounding layout.

techniques.name: ASCII Motion
techniques.does: An image becomes a grid of brightness-mapped characters, and the grid tightens until it resolves into the original.
use_when: In dev-tool, AI, or code intros where an image should show as characters
For a transition where characters resolve into the real picture

techniques.name: Atmospheric Depth
techniques.does: Distant objects look hazy and faint in fog, then sharpen as they come closer.
use_when: Stack background layers for a deep hero.
Let a subject sharpen as the camera advances.
Push out-of-focus layers back to emphasize the subject.

techniques.name: Attention Lines
techniques.does: An animation that connects one token to the tokens it references using arcs of varying thickness and opacity.
use_when: When explaining attention weights
When showing which preceding words receive attention

techniques.name: Audio Reactive Pulse
techniques.does: Shape size and glow intensity follow the low or high frequency strength of the sound.
use_when: Need sound-reactive elements in a music video or logo intro.
Let a background glow breathe with the music.

techniques.name: Audio Spectrum Visualizer
techniques.does: Bars or radial lines change length using precomputed audio band samples.
use_when: Visualize frequency-band energy in audio.
Keep the encoded values, labels, and visual state synchronized.

techniques.name: Audio Waveform
techniques.does: A line changes over time to display the amplitude of an audio signal.
use_when: Show speech intensity beneath an interview excerpt.
Display the amplitude of a soundtrack alongside playback.

techniques.name: Axis Rescaling
techniques.does: Ticks and gridlines move to a new scale as marks update with them.
use_when: Use when explaining axis rescaling in a presentation or interactive view.
Use when viewers need to track corresponding items between states.

techniques.name: Back Entrance
techniques.does: A small translucent element travels in, then settles at full size and opacity.
use_when: Bring a hero card in from a distance.
Focus attention on one main element in a scene.

techniques.name: Band Slide
techniques.does: Video bands split horizontally or vertically slide at slightly different timings to reveal the next screen.
use_when: When switching a list, table, or row-structured screen line by line
To create a tidy rhythm in presentation section transitions

techniques.name: Bar Chart Race
techniques.does: Bar lengths and vertical ranks interpolate between time steps.
use_when: Compare changing ranks over time.
Keep the encoded values, labels, and visual state synchronized.

techniques.name: Bar Grow

use_when: When showing differences in candidate probabilities and ranking
When comparing next-word candidate probabilities by length on a shared scale

techniques.name: Bar Wave Loader
techniques.does: Adjacent bars rise and fall in a staggered wave.
use_when: Indicate that voice processing is active.
Use a short repeating motion to communicate suggests signal processing and a steady work rhythm.

techniques.name: Barrel Lens Warp
techniques.does: Straight lines at the screen edge curve and the whole image bulges like a wide-angle lens.
use_when: Add a lens feel to a screen recording or UI screenshot.
Add a bulging wide-angle effect just before a transition.

techniques.name: Beam Collision Burst
techniques.does: A falling beam bursts into small light fragments the instant it hits the floor or a boundary.
use_when: Announce with a burst that data or a request has reached its target.
Use a falling line hitting the floor as the pivot that opens the next scene.

techniques.name: Beat Synchronization
techniques.does: Arrivals, scale changes and cuts land exactly on specific beats of the music.
use_when: Cards or lines appear in sequence over music.
Time cuts to the beat to strengthen rhythm.

techniques.name: Beeswarm Settling

use_when: Use when you need to explain beeswarm settling while preserving item identities and chart scales.
Use when the audience needs to follow the intermediate states rather than only compare final snapshots.

techniques.name: Bend
techniques.does: An object is anchored at one end, bends and sways, then springs back.
use_when: Plants, ribbons, thin paper or antennas.
A fixed-end element hit by wind or impact.
Emphasize by bending an object lightly and restoring it.

techniques.name: Blinds Reveal
techniques.does: Staggered strips open to assemble a complete image.
use_when: Use when presenting blinds reveal in a content reveal scene.
Use for a focused title, image, or card with a clearly visible final state.

techniques.name: Blink
techniques.does: An element's brightness or opacity switches on and off repeatedly.
use_when: Use on small indicators such as recording, live or warnings.
Show a cursor or input position.

techniques.name: Bloom Pulse
techniques.does: Soft light spreads around a bright object and then contracts.
use_when: When a logo or key object should glow at the climax
When neon or glowing UI should be stressed on the beat

techniques.name: Blur Dissolve
techniques.does: Two scenes overlap while blurred, swap, and the new scene sharpens back into focus.
use_when: Bridge a time skip or location change smoothly.
Join two shots of a similar tone without a hard cut.

techniques.name: Blur Resolve
techniques.does: A blurred target sharpens as its blur radius falls, pulling the eye.
use_when: When a title or product shot arrives as if focusing
When the background stays soft and only the target sharpens

techniques.name: Blur Reveal
techniques.does: Blurred text or imagery resolves into sharp focus.
use_when: Use when presenting blur reveal in a content reveal scene.
Use for a focused title, image, or card with a clearly visible final state.

techniques.name: Blurred Slide
techniques.does: A stretched blurred element moves into place and resolves to its normal shape.
use_when: Show a product moving rapidly.
Focus attention on one main element in a scene.

techniques.name: Boid Flocking
techniques.does: Small agents keep their distance, align heading and turn together as one flock.
use_when: Visualize self-organization, emergence and multi-agent ideas.
Create a backdrop that suggests agents cooperating.

techniques.name: Bomb Exit
techniques.does: An element tilts sideways, moves away, and disappears into a heavy blur.
use_when: Show a game prop being forcefully removed.
Focus attention on one main element in a scene.

techniques.name: Boolean Path Merge
techniques.does: Overlapping shapes join, or their intersection is cut out, forming a single silhouette.
use_when: Explain union and intersection in a Venn diagram.
Two logo shapes combining into a new mark.
Show cutting a window or hole out of a shape.

techniques.name: Border Reveal
techniques.does: A border line closes in from outside the element to reveal its outline.
use_when: When a form field or card becomes selected
When pointing at the edge of an on-screen element

techniques.name: Bounce Attention
techniques.does: An element bounces up and down in place, then returns to its original position.
use_when: Nudge people to press a button or notification icon.
Announce a newly added list item.

techniques.name: Bounce Landing
techniques.does: An object accelerates down, then bounces lower each time until it rests.
use_when: An icon or card drops from above and settles.
Announce arrival or completion with a lively touch.

techniques.name: Bounce Transition
techniques.does: The scene boundary drops, bounces off the floor several times with a trailing shadow, and reveals the new scene.
use_when: When dropping a scene in to cover the old one in a casual, bright explainer
When a product card bounces in from below to open the next section

techniques.name: Boxplot Update

use_when: Use when explaining boxplot update in a presentation or interactive view.
Use when viewers need to track corresponding items between states.

techniques.name: Branch Growth

To draw a background diagram as a metaphor for growth or expansion

techniques.name: Breathing Loop

Use for a compact status indicator with a stable surrounding layout.

techniques.name: Brush-linked Update

Explain intermediate values and selected ranges in a scroll-driven data story.

techniques.name: Animated Bubble Time Series

use_when: Use when you need to explain animated bubble time series while preserving item identities and chart scales.
Use when the audience needs to follow the intermediate states rather than only compare final snapshots.

techniques.name: Bulge Lens
techniques.does: A transparent lens sweeps across an image and bulges only the region beneath it.
use_when: Point out details inside an image one after another.
Sweep across a product photo to show surface texture.

techniques.name: Bump Chart Reveal
techniques.does: Rank trajectories unfold over time, crossing as items exchange positions.
use_when: Use when you need to explain bump chart reveal while preserving item identities and chart scales.
Use when the audience needs to follow the intermediate states rather than only compare final snapshots.

techniques.name: Burn Transition

use_when: Mark the turning point from an old way to a new one in a story.
Open or climax a piece that needs a tactile, dramatic texture.

techniques.name: Camera Fly-through
techniques.does: Move the camera through connected positions while directing its gaze toward the destination.
use_when: Connect separated information cards through space.
Travel through a tunnel to the next scene.

techniques.name: Camera Fly-through
techniques.does: A camera flies through seven planes spaced 900px apart and stops on the final keyword.
use_when: Travel through layers of information to reach a conclusion.
Show forward progress from input to output.

techniques.name: Camera Follow
techniques.does: Follow a moving subject by shifting the world in the opposite direction.
use_when: Keep the caret visible during long input.
Follow the latest section of a moving time series.

techniques.name: Camera Orbit

use_when: Reveal the front and side of a product.
Bring a globe destination to the front.

techniques.name: Camera Shake

use_when: Emphasize the instant after a collision.
Add a brief handheld feel.

techniques.name: Caption Page Swap
techniques.does: One or two lines of caption swap wholesale in a fixed bottom slot, timed to each utterance.
use_when: Basic captions on interviews, lectures and narration
Showing dialogue over busy footage without distraction

techniques.name: Caption Takeover
techniques.does: The usual caption line swaps for a huge full-frame title for one beat, then returns to the reading rail.
use_when: When the single most important sentence should fill the frame
When a plain caption video needs a rhythmic peak

techniques.name: Card Flip
techniques.does: A card rotates 180 degrees around its vertical or horizontal axis to swap front for back.
use_when: Flip a question card to reveal the answer.
Contrast two states of one object, such as before and after.
Move from a product card's name on the front to its specs on the back.

techniques.name: 3D Card Flip Stack
techniques.does: Five overlapping paper sheets flip in sequence and stack behind a frontal final card.
use_when: Reveal the result of a five-step sequence.
Show selection by turning editorial paper sheets.

techniques.name: Card Stack Shuffle
techniques.does: A rear card travels over the stack and settles at the front.
use_when: Reorder overlapping cards.
Show cycling recommendations.

techniques.name: Carousel Slide
techniques.does: A card rail decelerates into the next centered selection.
use_when: Browse product cards.
Emphasize the selected item in the center.

techniques.name: Cartogram Transition

use_when: Use when explaining cartogram transition in a presentation or interactive view.
Use when viewers need to track corresponding items between states.

techniques.name: Caustic Light Ripples
techniques.does: A bright net of refracted light drifts, concentrates and disperses as if beneath water or glass.

Lay moving water light on the floor beneath a product.

techniques.name: Cellular Automaton Evolution

Lay a slowly growing pattern over a grid background.

techniques.name: Connected Change Arrows

Use when the audience needs to follow the intermediate states rather than only compare final snapshots.

Get a gentler color-split effect than a glitch.

At chapter changes to show where the viewer is

techniques.name: Per-character Rise

Add rhythm to a sentence's entrance.

techniques.name: Chart Scrub

Keep the encoded values, labels, and visual state synchronized.

techniques.name: Chasing Dots

techniques.name: Chat Thread

techniques.name: Chomp Loader

techniques.name: Choropleth Transition

techniques.name: Circular Dot Wave

techniques.name: Particle Scatter & Assemble
techniques.does: Hundreds of particles floating across the frame fly in and assemble into one large number.
use_when: Reveal a key number or logo at full scale in an opening shot.
Show scattered samples converging into one result figure.
Set up a chapter number after a transition.

techniques.name: Particle Burst
techniques.does: Particles explode outward from a single point, fall under gravity, and fade out.
use_when: To mark an achievement like a click, payment done, or goal reached
To add an explosive accent where a logo or number appears

techniques.name: Particle Filled Text
techniques.does: Small dots inside letter shapes keep moving while still forming the strokes.
use_when: Rendering an AI, data or life-themed title as particles
Opening-logo style titles in brand films

techniques.name: Particle Force Field
techniques.does: Particles feel attraction, repulsion, and rotation forces, curving around a center and leaving trails.
use_when: To explain gravity, magnetism, attraction, and repulsion
For intro backgrounds with a force center

techniques.name: Particle Fountain
techniques.does: Particles shoot up from a narrow floor outlet and fall in parabolic arcs.
use_when: Show data, traffic or tokens flowing out continuously.
Build an intro where energy rises from a single point on the floor.

techniques.name: Particle image reveal
techniques.does: Scattered particles gather into the shape and color of an image and reveal it.
use_when: To reveal a logo or product image dramatically in an intro
To have particles converge into the next scene during a transition

techniques.name: Particle Life Clusters
techniques.does: Particles of several colors attract and repel by color, forming membrane-wrapped clusters or chasing blobs.
use_when: Use as a diagram background to explain emergence or self-organization.
Feature the particle system itself as the subject.

techniques.name: Connected Particle Network
techniques.does: Moving dots connect with nearby ones by lines that vanish as they drift apart.
use_when: Build a hero background themed on AI, networks or connection.
Abstractly show relations forming and breaking between nodes.

techniques.name: Particle Painting Advection
techniques.does: Short brush marks carrying the image's colors move along a flow field and scatter the picture like a painting.
use_when: Stage the moment a photo turns into a painting.
Build an intro where an image scatters and then reassembles.

techniques.name: Particle Video Mosaic
techniques.does: A fixed grid of dots takes its colors from the video frame by frame, redrawing the moving scene as points.
use_when: Explain visually that video is built from point-sized data.
Give a transition a dot grid texture that sets a digital tone.

techniques.name: Particle Vortex
techniques.does: Particles spiral toward or away from a center in a vortex.
use_when: Show many elements converging on one core.
Use a particle flow as the central visual of a loading or transformation moment.

techniques.name: Path Beam
techniques.does: A short luminous segment travels along a connector toward an active node.
use_when: Highlight a processing path.
Keep the encoded values, labels, and visual state synchronized.

techniques.name: Path Conveyor
techniques.does: Small objects travel repeatedly along a conveyor-like route.
use_when: Explain a repeating production queue with objects on a shared route.
Use a short repeating motion to communicate shows staged processing and production flow.

techniques.name: Path Convoy
techniques.does: Objects follow the same path with staggered starts or fixed spacing.
use_when: Show packets traveling along a network route.
Trace a procession of units through a logistics path.

techniques.name: Path Highlight
techniques.does: Only a short bright stretch travels along the full line.
use_when: When showing flow direction in a data pipeline or network
When light should circle the border of a card or panel

techniques.name: Percent Normalization
techniques.does: Stacks with different totals become equal-length bars while preserving their internal proportions.
use_when: Compare the composition of groups with different totals.
Switch an absolute stacked chart to a 100 percent view.

techniques.name: Perforated Tear
techniques.does: A section of a ticket tears along a perforation and drops away while the body stays.
use_when: Tear a stub off to mark a ticket as used.
Rip off a coupon or receipt in a scene.
Show part of a card's information detaching.

techniques.name: Perspective Flatten
techniques.does: A screen that starts tilted and small rotates flat to face the viewer and grows.
use_when: Introduce an app screen from a tilted pose to front-on.
A preview card flattening into the main view as you scroll.
Enlarge a product capture into a hero reveal.

techniques.name: Perspective Grid Drift
techniques.does: Grid lines converging toward the horizon flow forward toward the viewer.
use_when: Add space and speed to an opening background.
The floor for a neon or retro toned video.
A quiet looping background behind text.

techniques.name: Perspective Panel Rotation
techniques.does: Long panels of different colors rotate around a central axis, fanning out at an angle with near faces appearing larger.
use_when: Put a moving color panel backdrop behind a product intro or title.
Create a sense of stage or exhibition space with the background alone.

techniques.name: Perspective Swap
techniques.does: Two scenes swap left-right and front-back like perspective cards, with reflections following.
use_when: When showing the moment two screens trade roles, such as old and new versions
When two cards trade places to indicate a rank or priority change

techniques.name: Perspective Tilt Reveal
techniques.does: An editorial page tilts back by 55 degrees to reveal its grid before returning to one frontal figure.
use_when: Reveal the full structure around a single figure.
Return from an information atlas to its key figure.

techniques.name: Phosphor Trail Dissolve
techniques.does: Trails of light from bright objects linger as the previous screen changes to the next.
use_when: To keep screen afterglow in oscilloscope, radar, or CRT-themed videos
For sci-fi transitions where bright UI or text seems to persist

techniques.name: Phrase Push Build
techniques.does: Each new word enters from the right and pushes earlier words left, keeping the whole phrase centered.
use_when: When building a short slogan word by word into a finished sentence
When showing one line of narration as rhythmic typography

techniques.name: Physarum Trail Network
techniques.does: Many agents follow the trails left by earlier ones, and the paths that remain thicken into a connected network.
use_when: Explain or allude to a network organizing itself.
Create a life-like network background.

techniques.name: Physical Exit
techniques.does: An element accelerates off screen while rotating or falling.
use_when: Use when presenting physical exit in a content reveal scene.
Use for a focused title, image, or card with a clearly visible final state.

techniques.name: Pie and Donut Update
techniques.does: Shares update by interpolating the start and end angles of each pie or donut slice.
use_when: Use when you need to explain pie and donut update while preserving item identities and chart scales.
Use when the audience needs to follow the intermediate states rather than only compare final snapshots.

techniques.name: Piece Assembly
techniques.does: Loose shapes move and rotate until they lock into a single logo or a gap-free arrangement.
use_when: A logo outro where the mark completes.
Modules clicking together into one system.
Tiles packing into a seamless layout.

techniques.name: Pinned Scrollytelling
techniques.does: A visual stays pinned while scrolling explanations change its internal state and emphasis.
use_when: Explain a code sample through four successive highlights.
Keep a diagram visible while prose describes its stages.

techniques.name: Pivot Relay
techniques.does: An element rotates around one corner, then hands the pivot to another corner and settles.
use_when: Make a card entrance that flips up on a corner and settles.
Move a shape as if it rolls.
Explain how a center of mass changes.

techniques.name: Pixel Sorting
techniques.does: Pixel rows are pushed by brightness into stretched vertical or horizontal streaks, a glitch-art effect.
use_when: To let an image dissolve into data-like streaks during a transition
For strong texture in music videos or experimental titles

techniques.name: Plane Transformation
techniques.does: A grid and its shapes deform under one shared coordinate transformation.
use_when: Use when explaining plane transformation in a presentation or interactive view.
Use when viewers need to track corresponding items between states.

techniques.name: Point-to-point Construction
techniques.does: Each new point travels from the previous point to its data position, extending the line.
use_when: Use when you need to explain point-to-point construction while preserving item identities and chart scales.
Use when the audience needs to follow the intermediate states rather than only compare final snapshots.

techniques.name: Polar Coordinates Wrap
techniques.does: A horizontally laid-out image rolls into a circular band, or unrolls back.
use_when: Show a time-axis bar transforming into a radial chart.
Turn a horizontal strip into a radial structure to reveal periodicity.

techniques.name: Pop-up Book
techniques.does: A book's pages open and folded paper structures rise up to form a scene.
use_when: Open a chapter with a book opening and building its scene.
Introduce a city or room as a paper structure.

techniques.name: Portal Reveal
techniques.does: A glowing opening appears and the subject passes through its edge toward the viewer.
use_when: A dramatic entrance for a new feature or character.
Move to another space through a single doorway.
Bring a hero logo out of darkness.

techniques.name: Process Loop
techniques.does: An actor or icon visits successive stages in a repeating process.
use_when: Explain causes and results using process loop.
Present corresponding elements in a readable sequence within the same view.

techniques.name: Progress Ring
techniques.does: A circular stroke fills to a target ratio with a synchronized label.
use_when: Show completion or a share of a total.
Keep the encoded values, labels, and visual state synchronized.

techniques.name: Progressive Blur
techniques.does: Blur grows toward the content edge so moving content fades away smoothly.
use_when: Smooth the edge where a scrolling list slides behind a header or bottom bar.
Blur the surroundings to create focus on the central content.

techniques.name: Progressive Disclosure
techniques.does: A sequential reveal that leaves earlier stages dimmed as each new stage becomes active.
use_when: When explaining the processing sequence from input to output
When directing attention to the current stage in a multistep process

techniques.name: Pucker and Bloat
techniques.does: Vertices and curves are pulled in opposite directions, turning a shape into a star or flower.
use_when: A circle sharpening into a star to suggest a sparkle.
A petal-like swelling icon entrance.
A UI cue where an activated shape becomes sharper.

techniques.name: Puff Reveal
techniques.does: An enlarged blurred element shrinks into focus, or expands and blurs away.
use_when: Reveal an image or logo softly.
Focus attention on one main element in a scene.

techniques.name: Pull to Refresh
techniques.does: A resistant pull reaches a refresh threshold, waits, and returns.
use_when: Explain a list refresh gesture.
Distinguish loading from completion.

techniques.name: Pulse
techniques.does: A short scale beat where an element grows slightly and returns to its size in place.
use_when: When pulling attention to a button or badge that should be pressed now
When showing an active state such as a notification dot or record indicator
When pointing at one icon during an explanation

techniques.name: Push-in
techniques.does: A camera move that slowly approaches a fixed focal point in a sentence or scene.
use_when: When focusing on a key word after showing the full sentence
When showing an important part of a product or subject up close

techniques.name: Push
techniques.does: An incoming scene pushes the existing scene out by the same amount in the same direction.
use_when: Move between ordered steps.
Show the spatial relationship when moving to an adjacent scene.

techniques.name: Quote Card Build
techniques.does: The quotation mark and lines appear in order and the attribution attaches last.
use_when: Show a single review or interview line as a card.
Quote a speaker on a slide.

techniques.name: Rack Focus
techniques.does: A focus shift that swaps sharpness between foreground and background subjects without changing their positions.
use_when: When transferring attention between foreground and background
When changing the relative emphasis of two subjects without moving the scene

techniques.name: Radar Chart Morph
techniques.does: Vertices move along fixed radial axes to form or update a radar profile.
use_when: Compare two profiles on five consistently scaled axes.
Update a performance profile after a product change.

techniques.name: Radar Sweep
techniques.does: A bright scan sweeps across an area and leaves brief highlights.
use_when: Show an active search.
Explain the order in which locations are detected.

techniques.name: Radial Menu Fanout
techniques.does: Icons fan out from a shared center along an arc.
use_when: Use this effect when you need to communicate: Shows that several actions belong to one tool.
Connect interaction states within a product demonstration.

techniques.name: Radial Speed Lines
techniques.does: Lines from the center burst outward briefly and vanish.
use_when: Emphasize the instant a key word or product slams onto the screen.
Pull attention to the center right after a cut.

techniques.name: Rain Streaks
techniques.does: Thin lines fall fast in one direction and leave small marks on the ground.
use_when: Build a gloomy or tense atmosphere behind a scene.
Make a cinematic intro such as a rainy city at night.

techniques.name: Raindrop Glass
techniques.does: Background appears magnified inside drops on the glass as drops merge and run down.
use_when: Show a city or scene beyond a rainy window emotionally.
Add a droplet texture to product glass or a screen for freshness.

techniques.name: Random Walk
techniques.does: Dots repeat short random steps, leaving irregular trails.
use_when: Explain diffusion, search or random processes conceptually.
Visualize Brownian motion in a statistics or physics lesson.

techniques.name: Rank Transition
techniques.does: Items move to new ranked positions while retaining their identity and encoding.
use_when: Compare ranked products before and after a metric update.
Change a leaderboard sorting criterion while preserving item identities.

techniques.name: Reaction Cut
techniques.does: After an event or line, the view cuts to the face or reaction of someone who saw it.
use_when: When showing an audience or user reaction right after a surprising result in a talk, interview, or demo
When attaching another person's reaction after a statement in news or shorts to underline emotion

techniques.name: Reaction Diffusion Growth
techniques.does: Small blobs spread, split and settle into stripes or a maze-like pattern.
use_when: Explain how local rules create whole patterns, as in animal coats, coral or fingerprints.
Let an abstract, life-like texture grow over time behind content.

techniques.name: Repeated Text Wall
techniques.does: One phrase is duplicated into many rows that fill the screen.
use_when: Extend a brand name or campaign line into a background pattern.
End a title by flooding the frame with the phrase.

techniques.name: Motion Retargeting
techniques.does: When the target changes mid-move, the element eases from its current position toward the new direction.
use_when: Demonstrate an interaction where the destination changes mid-move.
Let live data updates continue from the current value instead of resetting.

techniques.name: Retreat and Cover
techniques.does: The previous scene shrinks and darkens while the new scene slides in and covers it.
use_when: Tell a story where new content stacks on top like layers.
Keep the previous scene in memory while moving on.

techniques.name: Ribbon-to-particle Transition
techniques.does: An aggregate ribbon dissolves into unit particles that travel along the same flow paths.
use_when: Use when you need to explain ribbon-to-particle transition while preserving item identities and chart scales.
Use when the audience needs to follow the intermediate states rather than only compare final snapshots.

techniques.name: Rigid Body Cascade
techniques.does: Many balls or boxes fall under gravity, collide, bounce and pile up on the floor.
use_when: Show many items pouring in and piling up, such as stock, alerts or data fragments.
Lead pieces resting on the floor into a logo or title after a transition.

techniques.name: Ring Zoom
techniques.does: Concentric rings show the footage at different magnifications, and the scene is replaced from the center.
use_when: Strongly gather attention on a central subject.
SF-style tunnel or warp looks.

techniques.name: Ripple Dissolve
techniques.does: Concentric ripples spread from one point, bending the frame while revealing the next scene.
use_when: Give a scene change a soft, physical quality.
Trigger the change from a click or touch point in UI demos.

techniques.name: Ripple Distortion
techniques.does: A circular ripple passes over the screen, briefly changing surrounding color and shape, then settles.
use_when: To show a response as a ripple at a click, activation, or landing point
For an image transition where waves sweep across the screen

techniques.name: Ripple Rings
techniques.does: Concentric rings expand and fade from a shared center.
use_when: Use when presenting ripple rings in a waiting or ambient scene.
Use for a compact status indicator with a stable surrounding layout.

techniques.name: Rising Bubbles
techniques.does: Translucent circles rise from below, sway, grow and fade away.
use_when: Lightly fill a background about water, drinks or cleanliness.
Give a loading or idle screen a soft upward motion.

techniques.name: Roll Reveal
techniques.does: An element rolls in or out through sideways movement and planar rotation.
use_when: Introduce a round icon playfully.
Focus attention on one main element in a scene.

techniques.name: Rolling Digits
techniques.does: Each digit rolls vertically inside a clipped number reel.
use_when: Update scores or prices.
Keep the encoded values, labels, and visual state synchronized.

techniques.name: Rolling Shape Loop
techniques.does: A shape translates along a floor while rotating in proportion to its travel.
use_when: Use a rolling shape to indicate repeated transport.
Use a short repeating motion to communicate suggests repeated work involving movement.

techniques.name: Rotation
techniques.does: Turns an element around a center point to change its direction.
use_when: When an arrow or expand icon turns with state
When rotating a card or diagram node 90 degrees to switch axis

techniques.name: Rotate Reveal
techniques.does: An element rotates in the plane while appearing or disappearing.
use_when: Give a badge a directional reveal.
Focus attention on one main element in a scene.

techniques.name: Rotate Scale
techniques.does: An element spins while growing, then settles back to its original size.
use_when: When a logo or icon should land with force
When showing a state change such as unlock or done with an icon

techniques.name: Rotating Plane Loader
techniques.does: A square flips around its horizontal and vertical axes in sequence.
use_when: Use a minimal geometric indicator during calculation.
Use a short repeating motion to communicate provides a simple repeating geometric waiting cue.

techniques.name: Rotating Tile Dissolve
techniques.does: Tiled copies of the frame rotate around the origin while the next scene blends in.
use_when: When blending scenes in a pattern-driven, graphic-heavy video
On beat-driven short-form cuts where the frame spins into the next shot

techniques.name: Round Corners
techniques.does: Sharp corners of a shape gradually round into curves, or return to sharp corners.
use_when: A square card turning into a button or circle.
A selected element softening as a state change.
The first step of a shape becoming a character.

techniques.name: Route Highlight
techniques.does: Nodes and links along a route light up in order from start to finish while the rest fades.
use_when: When tracing one path such as a customer journey or money flow
When showing a chosen prerequisite chain in a dependency graph

techniques.name: Sankey Reflow
techniques.does: Ribbon widths, node heights, and connected endpoints change together as flow values update.
use_when: Use when you need to explain sankey reflow while preserving item identities and chart scales.
Use when the audience needs to follow the intermediate states rather than only compare final snapshots.

techniques.name: Sankey Ribbon Growth
techniques.does: Flow ribbons grow from source toward destination, revealing the network stage by stage.
use_when: Use when you need to explain sankey ribbon growth while preserving item identities and chart scales.
Use when the audience needs to follow the intermediate states rather than only compare final snapshots.

techniques.name: Scale
techniques.does: Changes size proportionally from an anchor so growth direction and amount read clearly.
use_when: When a card or modal grows slightly as it appears
When a button dips and returns on press
When drawing bars that grow along one axis

techniques.name: Scale Pop
techniques.does: An element grows from a small scale to its final size.
use_when: Use when presenting scale pop in a content reveal scene.
Use for a focused title, image, or card with a clearly visible final state.

techniques.name: Scale Swap
techniques.does: The old element shrinks toward a pivot while the new one grows in to take its place.
use_when: Change an icon, card, or button into another state.
Swap one scene for another in the same position.

techniques.name: Scatter Dimension Rotation
techniques.does: Scatter points spread in depth, rotate, and regroup into the plane of a new variable pair.
use_when: Swap an X-Y scatter to X-Z axes.
Explain the result of dimensionality reduction or PCA.

techniques.name: Scene Integrated Title
techniques.does: The title is revealed and hidden in step with lines or character paths inside the scene.
use_when: Let a title pass behind an object in an opening.
Align letters with lines such as columns or buildings as they appear.

techniques.name: Screen Emergence
techniques.does: A tilted device screen flattens to face front, then the content inside scales up beyond the frame.
use_when: Move focus from a laptop or phone mockup to the app screen.
Reveal what is inside a device as the page scrolls.
Cut from hardware to software in a product intro.

techniques.name: Screen Shake
techniques.does: The screen or a word trembles side to side briefly and quickly settles.
use_when: Land a heavy word or an impact moment.
Signal a warning or error briefly.

techniques.name: Scribble Wipe
techniques.does: Scribble strokes stack up quickly to cover the frame, then wipe away to show the next scene.
use_when: Change scenes in a hand-drawn, notebook, or sticker-styled video.
Hide a cut behind the covering moment.

techniques.name: Scroll Frame Scrubbing
techniques.does: Scroll progress scrubs an image sequence forward and backward.
use_when: Letting viewers explore a product rotation or exploded view by scrolling.
Synchronizing explanation stages and video frames to the same progress value.

techniques.name: Scroll Grid Expansion
techniques.does: A pinned image grid enters by column, expands, and reveals supporting text.
use_when: Use this effect when you need to communicate: Moves attention from a collection toward a key scene.
Connect interaction states within a product demonstration.

techniques.name: Scroll Lag
techniques.does: After the scroll position changes, the screen and some layers trail behind and then settle.
use_when: Let background and foreground follow scroll at different rates for depth.
Smooth rough wheel input.

techniques.name: Scroll Scrubbing
techniques.does: Moving the scroll position forward or backward advances or rewinds the scene at the same ratio.
use_when: Bind step-by-step explanation to scroll length so people read at their own speed.
Let viewers scrub a product rotation or diagram back and forth.

techniques.name: Scroll-scrub Cinema Scene
techniques.does: In one pinned scene, a single scroll progress value p drives a title mask reveal, an assembling diagram, and a parallaxing background number together.
use_when: Use when a scroll deck pins one scene and assembles its parts step by step.
Use when showing or pitching a scroll-linked scene as video.
Use when speed differences between title, diagram, and background layers should add depth.

techniques.name: Scroll Snap
techniques.does: Scrolling settles smoothly at the nearest chapter boundary.
use_when: Use this effect when you need to communicate: Creates clear sections and stable reading stops.
Connect interaction states within a product demonstration.

techniques.name: Secant-to-tangent Convergence
techniques.does: Two points on a curve approach each other as their secant approaches a tangent.
use_when: Explain causes and results using secant-to-tangent convergence.
Present corresponding elements in a readable sequence within the same view.

techniques.name: Seek and Arrive
techniques.does: An agent turns toward a target and slows down as it approaches.
use_when: Explain how an autonomous agent approaches a target.
Show a pointer or robot slowing down near its destination.

techniques.name: Seesaw Balance
techniques.does: A beam tilts around a shared fulcrum while its pans counter-rotate.
use_when: Compare the weight of two choices.
Keep the encoded values, labels, and visual state synchronized.

techniques.name: Segmentation Reveal
techniques.does: A scan progressively reveals predefined colored region masks.
use_when: Explain region-level image analysis.
Keep the encoded values, labels, and visual state synchronized.

techniques.name: Segmented Explanation
techniques.does: A long process is split into short bursts of motion, each followed by a still hold.
use_when: When explaining a process of 4 or more steps in video
When a scroll deck should stop at each step

techniques.name: Selection Travel
techniques.does: A translucent selection band moves from one range to the next, resizing to fit.
use_when: When walking through code lines or tokens one by one
When a chart's period range is moved along section by section

techniques.name: Sequence Message Draw
techniques.does: Message arrows draw between actors in chronological order, highlighting each receiver.
use_when: Explain a client, server, and database exchange.
Trace an approval request through several roles.

techniques.name: Shader Directional Warp Wipe
techniques.does: A soft, bent diagonal edge sweeps across the frame while both plates near the edge stretch and smear along the direction of travel.
use_when: Cut from a sentence plate to a large-number plate with force.
Alternate light and dark scenes in sequence.
Add speed to a chapter-break transition.

techniques.name: Shadow Elevation
techniques.does: As an object rises off the surface, its shadow widens and fades, revealing how high it floats.
use_when: Select or lift a card.
Show a button hover state.
Show the height change when a drag starts and ends.

techniques.name: Shake
techniques.does: An element oscillates on both sides of its rest position or angle, then stops.
use_when: Shake a form field to signal an input error.
Get a notification icon noticed.

techniques.name: Shape Built Letters
techniques.does: Lines and geometric pieces slide together to complete the strokes and ornaments of letters.
use_when: Build a brand word out of shapes as its entrance.
Open with a typographic-poster feel.

techniques.name: Morph
techniques.does: The same element changes shape and color to become a component of the next scene.
use_when: Transform an input shape into a bar in output data.
Carry the same object across scenes in a different role.

techniques.name: Shape Repeater
techniques.does: The same shape multiplies with steady offsets in position, rotation and scale.
use_when: Radial patterns or logo decoration.
One shape multiplying into a grid or spiral.
Illustrate regular growth as a concept.

techniques.name: Shape Split and Merge
techniques.does: One shape splits into several smaller shapes, or several shapes merge into one.
use_when: Explain a whole dividing into three components.
Show several items merging into one category.

techniques.name: Shatter
techniques.does: A screen or word cracks into triangular shards that spin apart.
use_when: Transition where an old way breaks and a new one appears.
Blow a title apart as it exits.
Reset the screen after a shocking fact.

techniques.name: Shatter Transition
techniques.does: The frame or object splits into small fragments that scatter and reveal the next scene; in reverse, fragments gather into the new scene.
use_when: Convey the collapse of an old way or a shocking reversal.
Openers or climaxes that need a strong visual event.

techniques.name: Shooting Stars
techniques.does: Thin light trails streak diagonally and fade out like meteors.
use_when: Add small motion to backgrounds themed on space, night or AI.
Give a static dark backdrop an occasional glance-catching moment.

techniques.name: Shot Reverse Shot
techniques.does: Opposite viewpoints of two speaking people alternate with speech and reaction.
use_when: When switching the frame as the speaker changes in an interview or demo dialogue
In story-style videos where two characters trade questions and answers

techniques.name: Silk Flow
techniques.does: Glossy cloth-like folds drift slowly while light and shadow flow along them.
use_when: Backgrounds for calm, high-end brands such as luxury, beauty or fintech.
Fill the space behind a product intro with a gentle grain of light.

techniques.name: Animated Size Encoding
techniques.does: Shapes change area in proportion to their data values.
use_when: Compare magnitudes while keeping positions fixed.
Keep the encoded values, labels, and visual state synchronized.

techniques.name: Skeleton Shimmer
techniques.does: A bright band travels across muted content placeholders.
use_when: Indicate that card data is loading.
Preview the layout of content that is still loading.

techniques.name: Skew
techniques.does: Slants a shape along an axis to suggest force and speed.
use_when: When giving speed to a title or bar entering fast
When cards lean and return with scroll speed

techniques.name: Slide
techniques.does: An element slides in from an edge or moves out of view.
use_when: Show where a side panel comes from.
Focus attention on one main element in a scene.

techniques.name: Slit Scan
techniques.does: Each row or column is sampled at a different time so the image stretches and curves like a wave.
use_when: For surreal transitions or time-warp scenes
To erase a person or logo through time distortion in a memorable way

techniques.name: Smash Cut
techniques.does: Two strongly contrasting scenes swap instantly without warning.
use_when: To reveal a messy outcome right after a grand plan and land the reversal
To jump from a quiet scene to a loud bright one for shock

techniques.name: Smear Frame
techniques.does: During a fast move, the object stretches along its direction of travel and snaps back.
use_when: When a swipe, swing or pop-out should hit in one or two frames
When a ball or icon crosses the screen with force

techniques.name: Smoke Plume
techniques.does: Soft blobs rise, grow, overlap and thin out into smoke.
use_when: Add an afterglow when something disappears or is burned away.
Layer smoke over heat or fire to add depth.

techniques.name: Smoke Ring Vortex
techniques.does: Smoke curls inside a doughnut-shaped ring while its outer edge wobbles slightly.
use_when: Wrap a soft ring of light around a logo or title.
Show a mysterious or generating state through the background.

techniques.name: Soft Body Jiggle

techniques.name: Tile Possibility Collapse
techniques.does: Each grid cell shows overlapping candidate tiles that commit one by one while neighbor options shrink, until the pattern is complete.
use_when: Explaining how an algorithm or generative model builds structure from rules
Visualizing how a procedural pattern is generated

techniques.name: Wave Interference
techniques.does: Grid dots move with different sine phases, creating bright nodes and empty regions.
use_when: To explain waves, resonance, or signal interference
To build a geometric, meditative background loop

techniques.name: Wave Warp
techniques.does: Letter outlines bend and sway like a sine wave while the sentence stays in place.
use_when: For titles in sound or voice scenes that need a sense of vibration
To render text on water or in heat haze

techniques.name: Whip Pan
techniques.does: A rapid horizontal sweep with horizontal blur and sharp deceleration settles into the next scene.
use_when: Move quickly from a question to a result.
Maintain speed and direction across consecutive scenes.

techniques.name: Wiggle
techniques.does: A continuous, irregular jitter in position or rotation.
use_when: When a still element needs a little liveliness
When showing a nervous character or a camera shake

techniques.name: Wiggle Loop
techniques.does: An irregular wobble reconnects smoothly at the loop boundary.
use_when: Bring hand-drawn elements to life.
Repeat a subtle background wobble.

techniques.name: Wind Wipe
techniques.does: The edge extends a different length on each line, like streaks blown by wind, to reveal the new scene.
use_when: Scene moves that need speed.
Add texture when a straight wipe feels stiff.

techniques.name: Wipe
techniques.does: A moving boundary progressively reveals the new scene behind it.
use_when: Present information in order from left to right.
Replace the entire scene while keeping the transition boundary visible.

techniques.name: Wobble
techniques.does: A wide left-right sway with tilt that shrinks in amplitude until it settles.
use_when: When a cute character or sticker reacts
When a bad input should bounce back lightly
When adding a playful emphasis in short-form video

techniques.name: Word Emphasis
techniques.does: A phrase changes color and scale within a stationary sentence while surrounding text fades.
use_when: Focus attention on a key phrase within a sentence.
Align visual focus with an emphasized moment in narration.

techniques.name: Word Pop Caption
techniques.does: Each spoken word pops in turn to form short caption groups.
use_when: Make TikTok or Reels style captions.
Emphasize key words in fast-paced speech.

techniques.name: Word Relay
techniques.does: One big word enters from the right, pauses at center, exits left, and the next word takes over.
use_when: When showing a 2 to 5 word slogan one huge word at a time
When delivering keywords in sequence within one scroll section

techniques.name: Word Rise Fade
techniques.does: Words rise slightly while shedding blur, settling into place one after another.
use_when: When revealing a one or two line explainer caption or subtitle softly
For the calm brand-tone opening line of a video

techniques.name: Word Slot Cycle
techniques.does: The fixed part of a sentence stays put while one word slot cycles through alternatives.
use_when: When showing many uses in one frame, such as "Build ___ with AI"
When a product headline rotates through audiences or features

techniques.name: Zig Zag Path
techniques.does: A smooth outline gains repeating sharp points or waves.
use_when: Serrated edges for badges and stickers.
Outlines for strong messages like warnings, sales or bursts.
Change a soft circle into a wavy border.

techniques.name: Zigzag Wipe
techniques.does: Interlocking zigzag block boundaries move to reveal the new scene.
use_when: To swap scenes in sporty, techy, or street-style angular graphic videos
For directional wipes in list-style slide transitions

techniques.name: Zoom Callout
techniques.does: An animation that enlarges a small UI value in an adjacent circular callout and connects both locations with a line.
use_when: When showing 62% from a small candidate list in a circular callout at 4.5 times the text size
When showing the location and value of a detail within the overall screen

techniques.name: Zoom Flash
techniques.does: The frame zooms in fast and a bright flash carries it into the next scene at the peak.
use_when: Change scenes on a strong beat.
Snap attention to a product or title.

techniques.name: Zoom Through
techniques.does: The opening in the letter O enlarges to carry the viewer through to the next scene inside it.
use_when: Use the inside of a title letter as an entrance to the next scene.
Move from an overview into details such as probabilities.

techniques.name: Zoom to Detail
techniques.does: A motion that centers and enlarges a specific coordinate in an overview diagram to reveal detail.
use_when: When showing details of one subject within a node diagram or map
When explaining a selected point after showing the overall structure

techniques.name: Zoom Wipe
techniques.does: Mid-zoom on the center, a straight edge moves across the frame and reveals the new scene.
use_when: Change scenes in videos with camera-move feel.
Add depth to a wipe.
